newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's ANC against "right-wing" view on labour.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ANC against "right-wing" view on labour.

text.p: South Africa's ruling ANC has reaffirmed a commitment to its economic plan but will avoid a "right-wing" solution to improving labour flexibility, Labour Minister Tito Mboweni said on Tuesday.
Mboweni said protecting workers' rights had been high on the agenda of a four-day party meeting to map out government policy for the next two years.

Economic analysts had hoped the meeting, which ended on Sunday, would tackle the tough issue of boosting flexibility in the labour market but the African National Congress's powerful trade union allies, Cosatu, fiercely oppose erosion of workers' rights.
"We want to ensure that we avoid a situation where we are driven to the right-wing view that favours deregulation of the labour market, that people remain without rights," Mboweni said.

He said President Nelson Mandela and top ANC colleagues at the talks defined "right-wing" as driving wages down, reducing job security and refusing to extend wage-bargaining council agreements to non-participants.

Mboweni said the meeting had recommitted the ANC to the macro-economic plan unveiled by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel in June that maps a market-friendly economic blue-print for South Africa over the next five years.
Plans to ensure targets in the plan are met are to be revealed by Mandela when he opens parliament on February 7 and by Manuel in his budget speech on March 12.
On privatisation, a process started in late 1995, Mboweni said at the opening of parliament Mandela would "establish a timetable so that the certainty is clear".

"This year should see faster progress in the restructuring of state assets," he said. The ANC leadership had agreed that unnecessary delays and the inability to meet deadlines was a "thing of the past".
